Markets.title: Lower crude, global stability to drive market growth in new Samvat: ANMI President Kamlesh Shroff
Markets.summary: India's macroeconomic environment is projected to grow by over seven percent, driven by falling crude oil prices and global stability. According to ANMI President Kamlesh Shroff, these factors will strengthen the rupee, attract foreign investors, and boost equity markets during the new Samvat.

Markets.title: Indian economy to grow faster, foreign capital returning to markets: NSE CEO Ashishkumar Chauhan
Markets.summary: The National Stock Exchange CEO reports that India's economy will grow faster due to strong macroeconomic fundamentals and effective fiscal management. Additionally, domestic financial savings have reached nearly USD 1.4 trillion annually while foreign capital is returning to the markets.

Markets.title: Muhurat trading: Sensex up 320 pts, Nifty crosses 25,100; Tata Steel, Sun Pharma among top gainers
Markets.summary: During the special Muhurat trading session, the Sensex rose by 320 points and the Nifty crossed the 25,100 mark. Tata Steel and Sun Pharma were among the top gaining stocks during the trading.

Markets.title: Diwali turned lucky for these 8 stocks! Investors' wealth more than doubled, returns soar up to 191%
Markets.summary: Despite the Nifty 50 dropping nearly 3% since Diwali 2025, eight BSE 500 stocks more than doubled investors' wealth. Aditya Infotech, HFCL, and Welspun Corp led this rally with returns reaching up to 191% over the past year.

Markets.title: Muhurat Trading 2026 Highlights | Closing Bell: Sensex ends Muhurat Trading marginally lower, Nifty below 25,000; Divi's Labs surges 7%
Markets.summary: During the 2026 Muhurat Trading session, the Sensex closed marginally lower while the Nifty finished below the 25,000 mark. Despite the overall slight market decline, shares of Divi's Laboratories surged by 7%.

Geo-Political.title: Surgeon having lunch near Krakow shooting undoubtedly saved officer's life, colleague says
Geo-Political.summary: A surgeon eating lunch near Krakow provided critical medical assistance that saved the life of a police officer. The officer had been shot while helping stop a Polish gunman from harming more people.

Geo-Political.title: Seven dead and more than 100 injured after trains collide in Egypt
Geo-Political.summary: Seven people died and over 100 others were injured after two trains travelling in the same direction collided in Egypt. Several carriages derailed outside the city of Giza as a result of the crash.

Geo-Political.title: Homes and temples glow across India to mark Diwali
Geo-Political.summary: Millions of people across India are celebrating Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights. The holiday is being marked with traditional sweets, fireworks, and the lighting of lamps on homes and temples.

Geo-Political.title: Iran executes three men for 'armed unrest' after January protests
Geo-Political.summary: Iran executed Hassan Dioband, Hamid Kazemi, and Reza Zanganeh for alleged "armed unrest" during anti-government protests earlier this year. The men were claimed to have participated in the demonstrations that took place in January.

Geo-Political.title: Houthis say at least 33 killed in Saudi air strike
Geo-Political.summary: A Saudi-led coalition air strike in Yemen killed at least 33 people, according to the Houthis. Saudi Arabia has not commented on the attack.

Geo-Political.title: 'Flat', 'tired', 'cynical': Unusually gloomy Kiwis deliver New Zealand's tightest election in years
Geo-Political.summary: New Zealand voters are experiencing low national morale and declining faith in politics, leading them to desert the major parties. This discontent has resulted in the country's tightest election in years.

Data & Insights.title: India's forex reserves fall $2.69 billion to $717 billion: Why RBI is selling dollars and what it means for the rupee
Data & Insights.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves dropped by $2.69 billion to $717.06 billion in the week ending October 30, driven by central bank dollar sales, fund deployment, and valuation changes. The Reserve Bank of India is actively intervening in the currency market to manage volatility and support the rupee.

Data & Insights.title: Iran war: IOC to buy crude, LPG carriers as Strait of Hormuz disruptions drive freight costs
Data & Insights.summary: Indian Oil Corporation plans to purchase crude and LPG carriers while exploring domestic shipbuilding to counter rising freight costs caused by Strait of Hormuz disruptions. This strategy supports the company's broader efforts to diversify crude supplies, build inventories, and strengthen its energy supply chain.

Data & Insights.title: The midterms give Fed more room to raise rates, mut maybe less reason to do so
Data & Insights.summary: Midterm election results suggest a slowdown in datacenter spending. This reduction in spending could help curb inflation and influence Federal Reserve interest rate policies.

Data & Insights.title: No fresh curbs on broken rice exports as India banks on steady paddy procurement
Data & Insights.summary: India will not restrict broken rice exports because domestic paddy procurement remains steady. The world's largest rice exporter previously banned these shipments in September 2022 before lifting the restriction in March 2025.

Data & Insights.title: Bond yield rise squeezes banks' Q2 treasury gains
Data & Insights.summary: Rising bond yields caused public and private banks to suffer treasury losses during the second quarter. This financial pressure is expected to continue impacting bank earnings through the December quarter.

Data & Insights.title: Internship scheme's new pilot gets more takers post rejig
Data & Insights.summary: About 40,000 candidates have joined the third pilot round of the PM Internship Scheme, which is 2.5 times the turnout of the first two rounds. This positive response has encouraged the corporate affairs ministry to roll out the full programme next year without any further pilot rounds.

India.title: Delhi-NCR Chokes On Diwali Night As Smoke Engulfs City, AQI Nears 400
India.summary: On Diwali night, heavy smoke engulfed the Delhi-NCR region, pushing the Air Quality Index (AQI) close to 400. Prior to this, the Commission for Air Quality Management had enforced Stage 3 of the Graded Response Action Plan across the area.

India.summary: Global headlines focus on rising geopolitical tensions involving Iran, Israel, and the United States. Reports also highlight ongoing political developments across the Middle East.

India.title: HD Kumaraswamy Claims IAS Officer Paid Bribe To Stop Transfer, Points To Minister
India.summary: Former Karnataka Chief Minister HD Kumaraswamy alleged that an IAS officer paid a bribe to prevent a transfer. He supported the claim by reading excerpts from a WhatsApp conversation involving an official named Shashikiran and pointing toward a government minister.

India.title: "Bangladeshis Lying In Wait": Suvendu Adhikari To Security Forces At Bengal Border
India.summary: BJP leader Suvendu Adhikari claimed that Bangladeshi nationals are waiting near the West Bengal border to cross over illegally. He stated that these individuals are watching the Border Security Force to find an opportunity to slip across undetected.

India.title: Delhi Air Quality Turns 'Very Poor' On Diwali, To Turn 'Severe'
India.summary: Delhi's air quality dropped to the 'very poor' category on Diwali. Officials forecast that the air quality will worsen to 'severe' on Monday due to celebrations, vehicular emissions, and stubble burning.

India.title: Video: Whale Washes Ashore In Goa's Mandrem Beach, Released Into Sea
India.summary: A small whale washed ashore on Mandrem Beach in Goa. A group of volunteers wrapped the animal in cloth and successfully dragged it back into the sea.

General.title: Nandy defends linking Erasmus student scheme to Remembrance Sunday after backlash
General.summary: Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy defended her decision to connect the UK's potential return to the EU Erasmus student scheme with Remembrance Sunday. She argued that rejoining the study and work program will help honour wartime sacrifice, despite facing backlash over the comparison.

General.summary: Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy warned the media industry that it must take abuse allegations seriously following the Russell Brand case. She stated that many individuals within the sector have approached her with similar concerns.
